for 100K battery units from an unnamed multinational drone systems provider, with deliveries scheduled for next year's H1, as the customer scales its use of Enovix cells manufactured at its TAA-compliant facility in South Korea.
Following successful initial deployment, the customer is expected to place follow-on orders for the program in H2 2027 and beyond, Evonix

said the latest order moves one opportunity from the previously reported $216M pipeline into backlog, and the company expects additional pipeline opportunities to convert into purchase orders in the coming quarters.
"Drone makers need high-performance batteries from a qualified, non-Chinese source now, and this order shows Enovix can deliver," Chief Revenue Officer Steve Bakos said.
